headline: MIROIR KEEPS GROWING: First Mining Gold Hits 5.26 g/t over 19.55m as Duparquet Discovery Expands in Abitibi
snippet: First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF) released September 10-11 drill results from its 2026 program at the Duparquet Gold Project in the Abitibi region of Quebec: hole DUP26-093 returned 5.26 g/t gold over 19.55 metres, including 7.58 g/t over 12.95 metres, from the Miroir discovery zone. The Miroir target was first identified in 2024 and has been systematically expanded through 2025-2026 follow-up drilling — strike length is now approximately 220 metres with mineralization open in multiple directions. The 2026 program targets 15,000 metres total. At $4,362/oz gold, Abitibi-hosted high-grade shallow zones with an established discovery growth pattern command attention from institutional allocators and M&A screens alike. The result confirms the Miroir zone is cohesive, expanding, and becoming a meaningful resource contributor to the broader Duparquet project.

headline: RECORD VAULT: Gold ETFs Drew $18 BILLION in August — Holdings Hit All-Time High 4,189 Tonnes, AUM Surges to $615B
snippet: Global gold-backed ETFs attracted US$18 billion in net inflows during August 2026 — the second-largest monthly inflow in value terms on record — per World Gold Council data published September 10. Holdings rose by 121 tonnes to a record 4,189 tonnes globally, while combined AUM climbed 16% to US$615 billion. Europe posted its single largest-ever monthly inflow at US$7.9 billion; North America logged its third-largest at US$7.7 billion; Asia contributed US$2 billion — the highest since February. The data signals a decisive institutional shift: investors are not just trading gold around FOMC events but structurally adding allocation ahead of the September 15-16 rate decision. For junior mining investors, record ETF holdings confirm the upstream demand underpinning $4,362/oz gold is institutional in character — not momentum speculation — and is unlikely to reverse on a single rate outcome.

headline: BANNERMAN LOCKS IN CONSTRUCTION MONEY: A$124M Placement Puts Namibia's Etango on Track for Q4 FID — CNOL Takes 45%
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) launched a fully underwritten A$124 million placement at A$4.00 per share on September 9, completing its funding package for the Etango uranium project in Namibia and targeting a final investment decision and commencement of full-scale construction in Q4 2026. The placement settles September 15; an additional A$10 million share purchase plan follows in October. China National Nuclear Overseas (CNOL) holds a 45% JV interest — purchasing 60% of Etango's output — while Bannerman retains 55% and operational control. Etango is projected to produce 3.5 million pounds of U3O8 per year for 15 years. The fully underwritten raise was completed with uranium spot near US$90/lb and long-term contract prices at 18-year highs around US$96/lb. For uranium investors, a successful institutional raise and a Chinese nuclear JV at these price levels confirm that strategic capital has priced in a long-term uranium bull cycle regardless of near-term Fed volatility.

headline: MOSS GOES DEEPER: Gold X2 Drills 173m at 0.89 g/t Au — 100m BELOW Pit, Still 180m Above the Deepest Hole
snippet: Gold X2 Mining (TSXV: AUXX) announced September 10 assay results from the QES Zone resource expansion at the Moss Gold Project in Northwest Ontario: drill hole MQD-26-474 returned 173.0 metres at 0.89 g/t gold, collared from the southern QES Zone flank and intersecting mineralization 75-100 metres below the current RPEEE pit shell. The key geometry: the result sits 180 metres above the project's deepest confirmed hole (March 2026: 117m at 1.21 g/t gold), meaning a 300-metre vertical corridor of gold-bearing shears exists but has not been drilled to depth. This QES Zone depth result is separate from the Span Prospect northeast extension (September 8), where 40.4m at 2.05 g/t confirmed a 2km lateral extension — Gold X2 is simultaneously expanding the 6.7-million-ounce Ontario gold system in two dimensions. At $4,300+/oz gold, an open-ended Ontario resource with confirmed growth both laterally and at depth warrants significant attention from investors tracking Canada's largest undeveloped gold districts.

headline: CATORCE ZONE WAKES UP: Luca Mining Drills 9.9m at 5.39 g/t AuEq at Tahuehueto Mine — First Holes Since 2008
snippet: Luca Mining Corp. (TSXV: LUCA) released September 8 assay results from the first surface drill campaign at the Catorce Zone within its operating Tahuehueto gold-silver mine in Durango, Mexico — the first holes drilled there since 2008. The standout intercept returned 9.9 metres at 5.39 g/t gold equivalent, including 1.0 metre at 27.56 g/t AuEq, from a target interpreted as a southern extension of the Creston Vein system that drives main production. For retail investors following producing junior miners, this result is a mine-life extension signal rather than a greenfield discovery: the Catorce Zone was considered a separate, underdeveloped vein system for 18 years, and this drill campaign is now confirming a structural connection to the mine's primary producing vein. High-grade AuEq grades comparable to main Tahuehueto production from a previously untested area could add meaningful strike length and resource life to an already-producing asset.

headline: NEWFOUNDLAND DRILL TURNS: Galloper Gold Starts First-Ever 7,000m Systematic Program at Glover Island
snippet: Galloper Gold Corp. (CSE: BOOM) announced September 8 that diamond drilling has commenced at its Glover Island property in Newfoundland & Labrador — the company's first systematic large-scale drill program. The ~7,000-metre, 30-hole NQ program follows a full technical review integrating historical drilling, geochemistry, structural mapping, and geophysics. Initial holes target the Kettle Pond South Zone (historical: 2.53 g/t gold over 21.3m) and the Lunch Pond C anomaly (historical: 54.6 g/t gold over 1.22m) — both high-priority but never subjected to modern systematic drilling. Newfoundland has emerged as a serious Atlantic Canadian gold address since the Atlantic Gold (acquired by St. Barbara), Maple Gold, and Sokoman discoveries demonstrated the province's potential. The historical grades at Glover Island's two lead targets are exceptional by any standard; this drill program will confirm or eliminate them as resource targets for the first time.

headline: CAMECO MATH DOESN'T ADD UP: Produces 19-21M Lbs — But Must DELIVER 29-32M Lbs in 2026. BofA Sees $130/lb by 2027.
snippet: Analysis from The Oregon Group connects Bank of America's $130/lb uranium price target for 2027 — 52% above current spot near $85-90/lb — to a structural warning from Cameco's most recent earnings: the world's largest public uranium producer expects to produce only 19.5-21.5 million pounds of U3O8 in 2026 but must deliver 29-32 million pounds to customers, relying on spot market purchases and inventory to bridge an estimated 10-million-pound gap. This means Cameco is itself a price-setting buyer in the same spot market where utilities are scrambling to cover supply: US utilities have secured contracts covering only 48% of requirements through 2035. Kazatomprom — responsible for approximately 22% of global mine supply — lowered 2026 guidance to 27,500-29,000 tonnes, a 10% reduction. The combination creates a verifiable supply deficit operating independently of any Fed rate decision, making uranium one of the few commodities where fundamental constraints and upward price momentum are simultaneously aligned.

headline: NOVEMBER 10 IS THE DATE: NdPr Posts First September Pullback in 4 Months — China Export Control Expiry Looms Large
snippet: The neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) complex — the critical permanent magnet metal for EV motors, wind turbines, and defence systems — posted its first monthly decline since May in September's opening benchmark: neodymium metal fell 2.54% to $141.79/kg, NdPr alloy dropped 1.98% to $131.02/kg, and praseodymium fell 2.37% to $150.69/kg on the SMM domestic China benchmark as of September 3. This ends four consecutive months of gains that took the complex up 40% year-to-date. The market's clearest single catalyst is now the November 10, 2026 expiry of China's current rare earth export control framework: a renewal or tightening would spike prices; a liberalisation would trigger a correction. The broader September market continues to diverge — germanium surged +10% on defence procurement while scandium fell -7.36% — confirming that selectivity within critical minerals is essential. For investors, the September NdPr pullback may represent a tactical accumulation window ahead of the November 10 regulatory binary.

headline: COPPER STEADIES: CPER Ends Week +0.36% After Thursday's $563/t LME Crash — Equity Miners Still Under Pressure
snippet: Copper markets posted a modest recovery to close out the September 11 session, with the CPER copper tracker gaining 0.36% to US$39.18, following Thursday's historic $563-per-tonne LME crash from the all-time record of $14,875/tonne. Individual mining equities remained weak: Southern Copper fell 0.33% to US$193.49 and Freeport-McMoRan slipped 0.20% to US$71.07. The underlying supply picture remains tight: H1 2026 world copper mine production fell an estimated 1.1% per ICSG data, Chilean output declined 5.8%, and DRC copper concentrate production was off 36% due to ongoing Kamoa-Kakula seismic recovery — confirming Thursday's record LME high reflected genuine physical tightness, not pure speculation. The binary into next week's Fed decision: a hike (90% odds) could soften risk appetite for copper further; a hold or dovish pivot would likely reignite the tariff-premium bid that drove the LME record.

headline: SUPPLY CAN'T KEEP UP: Global Gold Mine Output Flatlines While Institutional Demand Accelerates on Every Front
snippet: A September 10 analysis highlights the structural mismatch powering the gold market at $4,362/oz: global mine production has essentially flatlined since 2018 despite record prices and rising exploration budgets, while demand has accelerated across every institutional channel simultaneously. Gold-backed ETFs just posted their second-largest monthly inflow in history ($18B, August 2026); central banks bought 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 alone, exceeding the five-year quarterly average; and total H1 2026 gold demand reached 2,522 tonnes at a record value of US$380 billion. The supply constraint is geological — average discovery grade per exploration dollar has declined steadily, and major mine grades are in structural decline. For junior mining investors, the confluence of record institutional demand and flat mine supply creates the most favourable fundamental backdrop for new discoveries and resource expansions in a generation: a new high-grade intercept in a proven gold district now competes for capital in an environment where the supply side cannot answer the demand signal.
